newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CLF, CCB spread up on French vote.
newsitem.headline: CLF, CCB spread up on French vote.

text.p: The discount of shares of French bank Credit Local de France against those of its Belgian partner Credit Communal (CCB) widened sharply on Monday, as CLF plunged with other French banks following the socialist victory in Sunday's elections.
CLF was down nearly five percent to 513 French francs (or 3,128 Belgian francs), while CCB was down only 1.3 percent at 3,470, widening CLF's discount to CCB to 9.9 percent.
Both shares should theoretically be at par, as both groups are in a 50-50 percent cross-shareholdership relation, each controlling half of the other's banking operations.
Mignon, Hanart, Declerck portfolio manager Alexander Pechovitch said he had a buy recommendation out on the Dexia group, especially on the French arm.
"The Dexia group is very well placed on the European market, it is one of those few companies with a true European image, they have the know-how, and a good market position," he said.
The Dexia group is focussed on credits to local public authorities. It recently acquired a stake in Italian bank Crediop.
CLF's discount, which had risen to 11.4 percent in early trade, narrowed to 8.8 percent by 0955 GMT.
